findings.finding: WRS.NTO and WRS.STO opcode encodings correctly match the spec: funct12=0x0D for wrs.nto (bits[31:20]=000000001101) and funct12=0x1D for wrs.sto (bits[31:20]=000000011101), both with SYSTEM major opcode 0x73, funct3=0, rs1=0, rd=0.

spec_citations.excerpt: Encoding: opcode=SYSTEM(0x73), funct3=0, rd=0, rs1=0, funct12=WRS.NTO(0x0d)/WRS.STO(0x1d)

findings.finding: trans_wrs_sto correctly checks ext_zawrs config flag, clears load reservation, updates PC, exits TB with DISAS_NORETURN. The immediate-exit behavior is compliant with spec norm:Zawrs_stall_terminate which permits implementations to 'occasionally terminate the stall and complete execution for any reason.' QEMU's zero-duration stall is a valid implementation choice.

spec_citations.excerpt: While stalled, an implementation is permitted to occasionally terminate the stall and complete execution for any reason.

findings.finding: trans_wrs_nto correctly gates on ext_zawrs, invokes gen_helper_wrs_nto to check mstatus.TW/hstatus.VTW (system-mode only), then falls through to trans_wrs_sto for the actual stall. The CONFIG_USER_ONLY guard is appropriate since user-mode emulation has no privileged CSR state to check.

spec_citations.excerpt: When the TW bit in mstatus is set and wrs.nto is executed in any privilege mode other than M-mode... it will cause an illegal-instruction exception. When executing in VS- or VU-mode, if the VTW bit is set in hstatus... and the TW bit is clear... it will cause a virtual-instruction exception.

findings.finding: helper_wrs_nto correctly implements the two spec-mandated trap conditions: (1) virt_enabled + (S/U-mode) + HSTATUS_VTW + !MSTATUS_TW → VIRT_INSTRUCTION_FAULT, matching norm:Zawrs_virtual_instr_excp. (2) priv != M + MSTATUS_TW → ILLEGAL_INST, matching norm:Zawrs_priv_illegal_instr_excp. Unlike helper_wfi, does not additionally trap U-mode when S-mode is present — matching the spec note that wrs.nto is expected to be used in U-mode.

spec_citations.excerpt: When the TW bit in mstatus is set and wrs.nto is executed in any privilege mode other than M-mode... it will cause an illegal-instruction exception. When executing in VS- or VU-mode, if the VTW bit is set in hstatus... and TW bit is clear... it will cause a virtual-instruction exception.

findings.finding: Zawrs ISA extension correctly registered with ISA_EXT_DATA_ENTRY requiring PRIV_VERSION_1_12_0. The QOM property at line 1260 is created with MULTI_EXT_CFG_BOOL and writable=true, and the extension is enabled by default in rva22u64 and rva22s64 profiles (lines 3183, 3289).

Correct dependency validation: Zawrs requires RVA (since WRS instructions depend on LR/SC from the A extension for reservation-set semantics). Enforces the spec note that 'The instructions in the Zawrs extension are only useful in conjunction with the LR instruction, which is provided by the A extension.'

spec_citations.excerpt: The instructions in the Zawrs extension are only useful in conjunction with the LR instruction, which is provided by the A extension.

findings.finding: KVM extension mapping correctly registers 'zawrs' → ext_zawrs via KVM_RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZAWRS, matching the KVM ABI defined in linux-headers/asm-riscv/kvm.h:181.

Disassembler correctly decodes wrs.nto (case 416 = 0x1A0, corresponding to funct12=0x0D shifted into bits[24:15]) and wrs.sto (case 928 = 0x3A0, corresponding to funct12=0x1D shifted into bits[24:15]), using rv_codec_none/rv_fmt_none as appropriate for these zero-register-operand instructions.
findings.snippet:
case 416: op = rv_op_wrs_nto; break;
case 928: op = rv_op_wrs_sto; break;

findings.finding: Linux-user hwprobe correctly defines RISCV_HWPROBE_EXT_ZAWRS at bit 48 and reports it based on cfg->ext_zawrs at line 9526-9527. The bit position matches the upstream Linux kernel definition.

Load reservation is cleared with tcg_gen_movi_tl(load_res, -1) after WRS completes. This prevents the TCG optimizer from incorrectly eliding subsequent LR instructions. The spec does not mandate reservation clearing on WRS — it only defines stalling behavior — but doing so is a safe implementation choice that has no architectural side effects since the stall duration is zero in QEMU.

Bool config field ext_zawrs correctly registered via BOOL_FIELD macro. No migration VMState entry needed since Zawrs defines no new CSR or architectural state — the existing CSRs (mstatus.TW, hstatus.VTW) are already covered by their own VMState entries.
